yttrium.name: Yttrium
yttrium.role: The rare earth in REBCO tape and its buffer layers

whyItMatters.text: Compact tokamaks use high-temperature superconducting magnets made from REBCO tape ("rare-earth barium copper oxide"). Faraday Factory's tape uses yttrium as the rare earth; Fujikura's uses gadolinium or europium. Both put a yttrium-oxide buffer layer under the superconductor, so yttrium is in the tape either way.

stages.name: Compact fusion developers using REBCO tape (CFS, Proxima Fusion, Energy Singularity)

security.text: Each developer depends on one or two tape makers. CFS buys from Fujikura and Faraday Factory Japan; Proxima Fusion from Faraday Factory Japan. Shanghai Superconductor says it supplied all the tape for Energy Singularity's HH70 tokamak and Jingtian magnet. Russian customs also record Energy Singularity sending a 14 kg sample of Hastelloy C-276 tape to S-Innovations in Moscow 'for testing' in January 2024.

people.text: CFS's public supplier page lists the tests it applies to suppliers: financial health, quality systems, experience, technical capability and compliance. It says nothing about human rights or where raw materials come from. We found no human rights or responsible-sourcing policy from CFS, Proxima Fusion or Energy Singularity covering magnet materials. No harm was found at the developers themselves.

stages.name: REBCO tape makers (Faraday Factory Japan, Fujikura, Shanghai Superconductor)

security.text: Faraday Factory Japan's recorded imports all come from Moscow. Its 2024 Japanese import entries describe Hastelloy tape 'with Al2O3, Y2O3, MgO, LaMnO3 layers' and tape with 'Mg, Cu, Ba, Y oxide layers and a silver surface layer'. One December 2023 entry was 140 kg of finished tape valued at ¥113.7 million. Fujikura and Shanghai Superconductor have no rare earth, target or substrate imports in Sayari.

people.text: Fujikura has had a Responsible Minerals Sourcing policy since 2019. It asks suppliers to avoid minerals linked to human rights abuses in conflict-affected and high-risk areas. Faraday Factory Japan describes its process (IBAD buffer layers, laser-deposited superconductor) but we found no sourcing or human rights policy. We found none for Shanghai Superconductor either. No reports of abuse at the tape plants were found.

stages.name: Moscow coating step (S-Innovations / SuperOx-Innovations)

security.text: Russian customs show what the Moscow plant buys to make its yttrium layers. An 'yttrium target' for sputtering came from Maru L&C in Korea (6.1 kg, January 2022). A lanthanum-manganite target (13.2 kg) and another sputtering plate came from Toshima Manufacturing in Japan the same month. CAN Superconductors in the Czech Republic sent four yttrium-barium-copper oxide laser targets in late 2020 (about 36 kg, about US$43,000) and a 15 kg sputtering target in February 2023 (US$38,951). Shenzhen Rearth (China) sent a gadolinium-barium-copper oxide target in 2020, and AMS Korea sent magnesium oxide for the buffer in 2023. No yttrium oxide, rare earth compounds or silver were recorded. Contract dates and subjects were not checked.

people.text: No reports of labour abuse at S-Innovations were found. The step matters because it erases origin: rare earth arrives already pressed into targets made in Korea, Japan, the Czech Republic and China, and the target makers' own rare earth suppliers are not in any record we could find.

stages.name: Yttrium oxide and sputtering/laser targets (Korea, Japan, Czech Republic, China)

security.text: Targets are the last place yttrium appears as a separate product. China has required export licences for yttrium since April 2025. By November 2025, European yttrium oxide prices were up 4,400% since January, at US$270/kg, against about US$7/kg inside China; licences covered only small shipments. Sayari shows Japanese yttrium-compound imports going to chemical firms and traders (Shin-Etsu, Sojitz, Toyota Tsusho), not to tape makers.

people.text: We searched for reports of forced labour, child labour or other abuse at the target makers (Maru L&C, Toshima Manufacturing, CAN Superconductors, Shenzhen Rearth) and at Japanese yttrium-oxide importers. None were found. Sayari holds no upstream suppliers for Maru L&C or CAN Superconductors; Maru L&C's only recorded imports are power-supply equipment from Malaysia. The risk at this stage is inherited: oxide made from Chinese-separated feed can carry Myanmar ore.

stages.name: Chinese heavy rare earth separators (China Rare Earth Group and subsidiaries, Ganzhou/Jiangxi; Fujian)

security.text: China Rare Earth Group, headquartered in Ganzhou, is a central state-owned enterprise; with China Northern Rare Earth it holds China's whole mining and separation quota. Global Witness found that its subsidiary China Southern Rare Earth said it had 'taken the lead' in importing Myanmar ore, and a customs official's research put its Myanmar share at 70% of raw materials. Plans for REGCC plants in Longling and Jianghua rely on Myanmar imports. Neither group is sanctioned.

people.text: Ore from Kachin and Shan enters these plants and leaves as Chinese oxide, so origin is lost here. We found no reports of forced labour or abuse inside the separation plants. Sayari holds no Myanmar-to-China rare earth trade records: a search for rare earth shipments leaving Myanmar returned none.

stages.name: Myanmar–China border crossings (Kachin and Shan to Yunnan)

security.text: Chinese customs data analysed by ISP-Myanmar show Myanmar supplied 60–87% of China's rare earth imports each year from 2017 to 2024. In January–September 2025 China imported over 28,000 tonnes worth US$624 million from Myanmar, 53% of its imports. Flows fell sharply when the Kachin Independence Army took the main mining belt; in October 2025 Beijing reopened four KIA-held border gates.

people.text: Rare earth revenue flows to armed groups: the Kachin Independence Army, the United Wa State Army and the NDAA. Both the KIA and UWSA were listed by the UN Secretary-General for recruiting and using children (2016 listing). Crossing the border turns conflict ore into Chinese imports.

harm.extremeBasis: S47: KIA and UWSA listed by the UN Secretary-General 'for recruitment and use' of children (2016); NEW1: KIA, UWSA and NDAA named as groups involved in the trade.
harm.reason: Rated severe: harm documented by 3 sources.
harm.note: Actor-level or single undated evidence: not used as the extreme-harm trigger.

stages.supplyReason: Over half of China's rare earth imports cross this border and flows swing with the fighting.

stages.name: Kachin State, Myanmar (Pangwa / Chipwi)

security.text: Myanmar is a major yttrium source (USGS). Global Witness found heavy rare earth oxide imports from Myanmar to China rose from 19,500 tonnes in 2021 to 41,700 tonnes in 2023, more than double China's own heavy rare earth quota.

people.text: 300+ mining sites in Kachin Special Region 1. Streams are acidic and contaminated. Workers, including a 15-year-old, have died after chemical exposure, and landslides killed at least 35 miners in June 2024. Workers report violence and sexual exploitation. Mines were run by a junta-aligned militia and since late 2024 by the KIA, which the UN listed for child recruitment.

harm.extremeBasis: S1: a 15-year-old among miners who died; S3: workers report physical violence and sexual exploitation.
harm.reason: Rated severe: child labour, violence against workers and sexual exploitation documented (5 sources).

stages.supplyReason: Large share of heavy rare earth feed, but output swings with fighting and border closures.

stages.name: Eastern Shan State, Myanmar (new UWSA-protected mines)

security.text: Reuters found new rare earth mines with leaching pools in eastern Shan State, built from 2023, operating under the protection of the United Wa State Army and run with Chinese operators. Myanmar supplied nearly half of China's imports in January–April 2025.

people.text: Reuters did not report specific abuses at the new Shan sites, and we found none. The protecting group, the UWSA, was listed by the UN Secretary-General for recruiting and using children. The sites copy the Kachin leaching method that has poisoned streams there.

harm.extremeBasis: S47: UWSA listed 'for recruitment and use' of children (2016). Actor-level, not site-level.
harm.reason: Rated moderate: harm documented by 1 source.
harm.note: Actor-level or single undated evidence: not used as the extreme-harm trigger.

stages.supplyReason: New and growing, but small and dependent on one armed group.

stages.name: Southern China ionic clays (Ganzhou, Jiangxi)

security.text: China restricted heavy rare earth mining in Ganzhou from 2016 for environmental reasons; Global Witness reports up to 16,000 people moved from Ganzhou to Myanmar to mine. Domestic output is capped by quota.

people.text: Chinese authorities put the Jiangxi cleanup at about US$5.6 billion, with 50–100 years to recover. We found no reports of forced or child labour at current Jiangxi mines.

harm.reason: Rated moderate: harm documented by 1 source.

stages.supplyReason: Quota-capped and largely replaced by Myanmar feed.

yttrium.bottomLine: The magnets at the heart of compact fusion depend on yttrium separated overwhelmingly in China, where ore from armed-group-controlled Kachin State is mixed in and its origin lost. The records show yttrium reaching the Moscow tape plant as finished targets from Korea, the Czech Republic, Japan and China, but no record shows which mine any of it came from. Harm at Kachin is documented; the link into fusion magnets is likely, not proven.

context.label: Magnet maker: Commonwealth Fusion Systems magnet factory (US)
context.text: CFS winds its own HTS magnets in a factory it spent seven years and hundreds of millions of dollars building. It now sells magnets to others: WHAM (University of Wisconsin) and, from April 2026, Realta Fusion in a deal it calls its largest. It licensed its HTS cable technology to Type One Energy in 2025, without (yet) building Type One's magnets. Tape comes from Fujikura (10,000+ km order), Faraday Factory Japan, and earlier Shanghai Superconductor (110+ km) and Moscow's S-Innovations (2022). One factory now serves three developers, so a disruption here spreads. No reports of labour abuse at CFS's magnet work were found. The human-rights exposure sits upstream, in the tape's yttrium and nickel. CFS has bought tape from a Moscow maker (2022) and a Chinese maker that Sayari flags as a modelled military end-user contractor. CFS publishes no supplier due-diligence policy for tape that we found.

evidence.scope: who supplies the tape and who buys the magnets

context.label: Magnet maker: Tokamak Energy (UK) in-house HTS magnets
context.text: Tokamak Energy built its own set of 44 HTS coils (Demo4) from 38 km of tape, announced February 2023. Tape came from several makers: Shanghai Superconductor supplied wide tape in 2017-2020, and Furukawa agreed in January 2023 to supply several hundred km made at SuperPower in New York for the ST80-HTS prototype. It is a DOE Milestone awardee through its US subsidiary. No reports of labour abuse at Tokamak Energy were found. Sayari holds no tape import records for it (UK import data is thin), so its current tape mix cannot be checked from trade data.

context.label: Magnet maker: Energy Singularity (Shanghai) in-house HTS magnets
context.text: Energy Singularity built the HH70, which in June 2024 became the first tokamak with all-HTS magnets, and its Jingtian magnet reached 21.7 tesla in March 2025. Shanghai Superconductor supplied all the tape for both. This is a fully Chinese chain from tape to magnet. No reports of labour abuse at Energy Singularity were found. Its tape maker, Shanghai Superconductor, was co-founded with investment from a Jiangxi business group (Jiangxi is the heart of Chinese heavy rare earth separation), per its registry business description. No record ties its yttrium to any mine.

context.label: Reactor / developer: Proxima Fusion (Germany)
context.text: Proxima plans a Stellarator Model Coil, its demonstration HTS magnet, for 2027. Faraday Factory Japan agreed to supply tape for its demo stellarator; Proxima's site also lists a Fujikura partnership on HTS manufacturing in Germany. We found no public statement on who winds its coils. No reports of harm were found. Exposure is upstream via Faraday Factory Japan, which received 369 shipments of tape from Moscow until January 2025.

context.label: Reactor / developer: Type One Energy and Realta Fusion (US)
context.text: Neither makes its own magnets at scale. Realta buys HTS magnets from CFS (WHAM's 17-tesla magnets in 2024; multi-year deal April 2026). Type One holds an exclusive licence to CFS's HTS cable technology (2025). Both are DOE Milestone awardees. Neither has named a tape supplier publicly that we found. No reports of harm were found. Their exposure runs through CFS's tape purchases.

nickel.role: The Hastelloy alloy strip that REBCO tape is built on

whyItMatters.text: REBCO tape is built on thin strip of Hastelloy C-276, a nickel-chromium-molybdenum alloy. Specialty mills market this strip directly to tape makers.

stages.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (shipper of bare Hastelloy to Moscow)

security.text: CFS sent 15 shipments of bare Hastelloy C-276 tape (about 29 tonnes) to S-Innovations from May 2022 to December 2024, and received coated tape back in early 2022. Where CFS buys its own C-276 strip is not in the trade records.

people.text: CFS's supplier criteria cover finance, quality, experience, technical capability and compliance; human rights and material origin are not mentioned. We found no CFS statement on where substrate nickel comes from.

stages.name: Moscow coating step: where its Hastelloy strip came from

security.text: Russian customs record 34 shipments of Hastelloy C-276 strip into the two S-Innovations entities from February 2022 to January 2025. 15 came from CFS (USA). people.text: No reports of labour abuse at S-Innovations or its strip suppliers were found. None of the Chinese suppliers has any upstream data in Sayari, so their nickel source cannot be seen.

stages.name: Hastelloy C-276 strip mills (Haynes, VDM/Acerinox, Chinese mills)

security.text: Haynes (which invented Hastelloy) and VDM Metals now both belong to Spain's Acerinox. Haynes buys nickel 'through an exclusive arrangement with a single supplier' it does not name, and melts virgin metal with purchased scrap. Sayari shows Haynes importing nickel scrap (53 records) from suppliers in the US, Germany, the UK and elsewhere. Acerinox's 2025 report lists 'diversification of nickel supply sources' as a goal but does not name origins.

people.text: VDM says it follows OECD due diligence guidance and belongs to the Responsible Minerals Initiative and the Metals Alliance for Responsible Sourcing, mainly for conflict minerals. Haynes's filing names no nickel origin. The Chinese mills publish nothing we could find. No harm was found at the mills; nickel from many mines is melted together here.

stages.name: Chinese nickel refining (fed by Indonesian matte)

security.text: China imported US$8.85 billion of nickel from Indonesia in 2025, US$8.15 billion of it as nickel matte (UN COMTRADE). Chinese alloy mills therefore draw largely on Indonesian feed, but no record links a specific mill to a specific smelter.

people.text: Matte from Morowali and Weda Bay is refined in China and mixed with other feed. We found no reports of abuse at Chinese nickel refineries in our searches; the documented harm sits at the Indonesian smelters and mines.

stages.name: Indonesian nickel hubs (Morowali, Weda Bay)

security.text: Indonesia mined an estimated 2.6 million of the world's 3.9 million tonnes of nickel in 2025, about two-thirds. Acerinox, owner of Haynes and VDM, reported nickel prices moving on 'regulatory uncertainty in Indonesia' and possible ore restrictions.

people.text: Indonesia's human rights commission found the state failed to protect rights around Morowali. A smelter furnace explosion killed 21 workers in December 2023. At Weda Bay, companies working with police and military took land through coercion and intimidation.

nickel.bottomLine: Sayari did not confirm the Indonesia hypothesis: no path links tape substrate to Morowali or Weda Bay. It found a different route instead. Hastelloy strip from the US, China and Japan-based traders went to a Moscow plant that coated it for a Japanese maker supplying fusion developers.

stages.name: Grasberg mine, Central Papua, Indonesia

Seven workers died in the September 2025 mud rush.

copper-hts.bottomLine: The copper in a fusion magnet can be traced further than most of its metals: CFS's copper conductor came from a Finnish maker that buys cathode refined from Indonesia's Grasberg mine, where security-force killings and tailings damage have been reported.

context.label: Sector-wide
context.text: Verisk Maplecroft (2017) rated tin the highest-risk of the 3TG minerals for labour rights violations, and rated child labour an "extreme risk" in Bolivia, Myanmar and Indonesia.

context.label: Magnet maker: ITER toroidal-field coil makers, Europe (ASG Superconductors, SIMIC, ICAS consortium)
context.text: ASG Superconductors (La Spezia, Italy), with Iberdrola and Elytt, wound Europe's 10 toroidal-field winding packs. SIMIC made radial plates, ran cold tests and inserted coils into cases. The ICAS consortium (ENEA, Tratos, Criotec) made Europe's cable-in-conduit conductor. ITER's 500 t of Nb3Sn strand (100,000+ km) came from nine suppliers, 2008-2015. No reports of labour abuse at these coil makers were found. Separately, Sayari shows ASG importing amorphous boron powder from AO Aviabor (Dzerzhinsk, Russia) in 2019 and December 2022, after Russia's full invasion of Ukraine. Boron is used in MgB2 superconductor, ASG's other product line, not ITER's Nb3Sn. Aviabor is not sanctioned in Sayari but carries a modelled military-end-user-contractor flag.

context.label: Magnet maker: ITER toroidal-field coil makers, Japan/Korea (QST with MHI, Mitsubishi Electric, Toshiba ESS, Hyundai Heavy)
context.text: Japan's agency QST supplies 9 toroidal-field coils plus 10 coil structures, with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi Electric, Hyundai Heavy Industries and Toshiba Energy Systems & Solutions. No reports of labour abuse tied to ITER coil work were found. Sayari shows forced-labour 'sub-tier' flags on MHI, Toshiba ESS and HD Hyundai Heavy; these are modelled from their whole trade networks, not from magnet work, and are not documented harm.

context.label: Magnet maker: General Atomics, ITER central solenoid (US)
context.text: General Atomics built the six central solenoid modules (plus a spare) at its Magnet Technologies Center in Poway, California; completion announced 28 August 2025. The solenoid is wound from Nb3Sn cable. No reports of labour abuse tied to the solenoid work were found. Sayari's forced-labour 'sub-tier' flags on General Atomics are modelled across its whole (largely defence) trade network.

tin.bottomLine: Fusion's Nb₃Sn strand makers are known, and one of them lists Yunnan Tin among its group's smelters; Yunnan Tin has said some of its tin came from the Wa State mine run by a US-sanctioned armed group. A second smelter in Malaysia buys from traders who also handle Rwanda's conflict-linked coltan. The harm is documented; the route into fusion strand is likely, not proven.

stages.name: Masan Tungsten APT plant, Nui Phao (Thai Nguyen, Vietnam)

security.text: Nui Phao produces almost all of Vietnam's roughly 3,400 t of tungsten a year; Vietnam was the world's second-biggest producer in 2024. Owner Masan has explored selling the business, and Reuters reported Chinese firms seeking a stake through proxies. Mitsubishi Materials took 10% in 2020, and US firm Elmet agreed in 2026 to buy 4.99% plus about 1,250 t a year of tungsten oxide. The mine licence runs to early 2028.

people.text: The plant sits inside the Nui Phao mining complex (see the mine stage for documented pollution complaints). Sayari tags the plant with forced-labour 'sub-tier' flags; these are modelled from network patterns, not evidence of forced labour, and we found no report of forced labour at Nui Phao.

evidence.scope: forced labour (Sayari flag is modelled; no reports found)

stages.name: Rwanda (Nyakabingo) and Colombia

security.text: Nyakabingo, 19 km from Kigali, is Africa's largest tungsten mine, producing 100-110 t of wolframite a month with 1,800+ workers. Colombian exporters sold ore to the US powder plant in 2012-13.

stages.name: Southern Jiangxi, China

security.text: China mined about 79% of the world's tungsten in 2025 and tightened export controls in February 2025. Southern Jiangxi (Ganzhou) is one of the world's main tungsten mining centres.

people.text: A 2024 peer-reviewed study found farmland and rice near tungsten mines in southern Jiangxi polluted with cadmium, arsenic, molybdenum and tungsten, with cancer and non-cancer risks above safe thresholds for arsenic and cadmium. No record names AT&M's ore suppliers, so a link from these mines to fusion parts is untested.

tungsten.bottomLine: Only a handful of firms make fusion-grade tungsten, and China mines about four-fifths of the world's supply. ITER's Japanese divertor maker buys its tungsten from a Vietnamese mine where residents' pollution complaints led to a government inspection. Nothing ties conflict-linked ore to a fusion part.

lithium6.name: Lithium-6
lithium6.role: Enriched lithium for breeding tritium fuel

stages.name: Fusion developers that need enriched lithium (e.g. Type One Energy, Gauss Fusion)

security.text: Fusion plants that burn deuterium-tritium must breed their own tritium from lithium-6. Pilot plants will need tens of tonnes of enriched lithium, commercial plants hundreds. There is no commercial supply yet; Type One Energy and Gauss Fusion signed supply deals with Molten Salt Solutions in March 2026.

people.text: Developers have no lithium-6 supply chain yet, so there is no current harm at this stage. The choice they face is between new non-mercury processes and the mercury-based process used in Russia and China.

stages.supplyReason: No commercial supply exists today.

stages.name: Molten Salt Solutions (US, new non-mercury process)

security.text: A Santa Fe start-up whose founders include Los Alamos scientists, with DOE INFUSE funding. It plans kilogram-scale deliveries from 2027, with a path to hundreds of tonnes.

people.text: Its solvent-exchange process avoids mercury. It is not yet producing at scale, so there is no operating record to assess. Sayari holds its registry records but no trade.

stages.name: Natural lithium: Australia, Chile, China, Argentina, Zimbabwe (and US projects)

security.text: Ordinary lithium is mined mostly in Australia, Chile, China, Argentina and Zimbabwe; US imports come mainly from Chile and Argentina. Enrichment, not mining, is the bottleneck for fusion. No source says where Novosibirsk or Molten Salt Solutions get their lithium.

people.text: Amnesty International reported in 2026 that lithium projects in Nevada, including Thacker Pass, were approved without the free, prior and informed consent of affected Indigenous Peoples. Whether any of this lithium will feed fusion enrichment is untested.

evidence.scope: Indigenous rights violations at US lithium projects

harm.reason: Rated moderate: harm documented by 1 source.

stages.supplyReason: Natural lithium is widely mined; enrichment, not mining, is the constraint.

stages.name: Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant (Rosatom/TVEL, Russia) and China

security.text: Only Russia and China enrich lithium today; China is reported to buy from Russia. Russia's Novosibirsk plant supplies up to 80% of the world's lithium-7, a by-product of enriching lithium-6 for weapons. It is on Ukraine's sanctions list (Sayari). Its supply is not known to be available to fusion developers.

people.text: The plant uses mercury electrolysis. It also has a radioactive tailings dump 7 km from Novosibirsk that Rosatom plans to close over the next decade. We found no public reports of mercury contamination or worker harm at the plant, but independent information from inside Russia's nuclear complex is scarce.

evidence.scope: documented harm to people (searched; none found)

stages.name: Oak Ridge, Tennessee, 1950s-60s (history)

security.text: The US enriched lithium-6 for weapons at Oak Ridge's Y-12 plant using the mercury process, which is now banned in the US.

people.text: Enrichment at Oak Ridge used mercury. About 1.1 million kg was lost on site, around 10% of it into East Fork Poplar Creek. About 15 miles of the creek still exceed mercury water-quality criteria.

harm.reason: Rated severe: harm documented by 3 sources.

stages.supplyReason: Historical; no longer operating.

lithium6.bottomLine: Fusion's fuel chain has caused harm before: lithium-6 enrichment at Oak Ridge left mercury in a creek that still exceeds water-quality criteria. Today the only producers are in Russia and China, one of them on Ukraine's sanctions list, and new enrichers are only now signing deals with fusion developers.

beryllium.name: Beryllium

stages.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (FLiBe) · EU DEMO solid blanket

security.text: CFS has a supply agreement with Materion for beryllium fluoride for its molten-salt blanket. Europe's DEMO design uses beryllium compounds (beryllides) as its neutron multiplier.

people.text: The main risk is lung disease for people who handle beryllium dust. We found no reports of harm at CFS or the EU blanket programme.

stages.name: Materion (US)

security.text: Materion mines bertrandite ore at Spor Mountain, Utah, mills it near Delta into beryllium hydroxide, and also buys beryl ore. It is CFS's supplier.

people.text: Breathing beryllium dust can cause chronic beryllium disease, which Materion's own filing says can cause disability or death. In 1998 the company (then Brush Wellman) settled lawsuits with workers who had contracted the disease. In 2023 the US Labor Department accepted a claim from a worker at the Delta, Utah mill diagnosed with beryllium sensitisation. Materion reported no pending beryllium cases at the end of 2025.

evidence.scope: occupational disease (court record, federal claim decision)

steel.name: Specialty steels
steel.role: Structural steels for the vessel and blanket

stages.name: ITER vacuum vessel and EU breeding-blanket structures

security.text: ITER's vacuum vessel is nine steel sectors; Europe supplies five, built by the AMW consortium (Ansaldo Nucleare, Mangiarotti, Walter Tosto) in Italy, and Korea the rest. Europe's test blanket modules use EUROFER97 steel.

people.text: We found no human rights issue reported at the vessel builders. Public procurement news describes the steel's chemistry (chromium, nickel) but not where those metals were mined.

evidence.scope: harm at this stage (searched; none found)

stages.supplyReason: Specialist heavy fabrication, but several qualified firms.

stages.name: ITER-grade stainless 316L(N)-IG: Industeel (France), ThyssenKrupp and Rolf Kind (Germany), Valbruna and Forgiatura Vienna (Italy)

security.text: For Europe's five vessel sectors, about 1,100 forgings (about 1,900 t) and 150 plates (1,120 t) came from these five firms. Industeel's Le Creusot works also shipped about 5,000 t of plate to India, 3,500 t each to Japan and Korea and 300 t to Russia for ITER parts.

people.text: We found no reports of rights abuses at these European mills. The steel is made by mixing chromium and nickel with steel; none of the sources say where those alloying metals came from, and Sayari shows no alloy purchases by Industeel.

evidence.scope: harm at the mills (searched; none found)

stages.name: Chromium: South Africa (Limpopo) and Kazakhstan

security.text: South Africa mined about 45% of the world's chromite ore in 2025 (23 of 51 million t) and Kazakhstan about 14%; 95% of resources are in Kazakhstan and southern Africa. China makes most ferrochrome.

people.text: Human Rights Watch and partners documented threats and violence against community activists in Limpopo's chrome-mining area. In July 2017 police and company security 'responded violently' to a protest near the Sefateng chrome mine, and a protester was hit by a rubber bullet; in 2015 protesters against the Chromex mine were injured by rubber bullets and arrested. For Kazakhstan's chrome mines we found no reports of abuses. No record shows which chrome went into fusion steel.

evidence.scope: violence against protesters at Limpopo chrome mines

harm.extremeBasis: "police and company security forces responded violently to another community protest near the Sefateng Mine" (HRW 2019, NEW13)
harm.reason: Rated severe: violence documented (1 source).

stages.supplyReason: Concentrated in two countries, but large reserves.

stages.name: EUROFER97 low-activation steel (blanket structures): Saarschmiede, Böhler

security.text: Europe's reference fusion steel has so far been made industrially by two firms: F4E's 27 t order was forged by Saarschmiede (Germany) with Böhler (Austria). It is about 9% chromium and 1.1% tungsten, with small amounts of vanadium (about 0.2%) and tantalum (about 0.12%).

people.text: No rights issue found at the forges. The alloying metals link this steel to other chains: tungsten (see tungsten), tantalum (mined alongside coltan in Central Africa, where conflict links are documented), chromium and vanadium (below). Sayari records no suppliers for Saarschmiede, because EU-internal purchases are not in customs data.

evidence.scope: harm at the forges (searched; none found)

sayari.name: Saarschmiede GmbH Freiformschmiede
sayari.basis: Registry: HRB 75004. Sayari records no suppliers (receives_from: 0); EU-internal purchases of alloying metals are not in customs data.

stages.supplyReason: Only two industrial producers so far.

stages.name: Vanadium: China, Russia, South Africa

security.text: China produced about 75% of the world's vanadium in 2025 (82,000 of 110,000 t), Russia about 19% and South Africa about 5%. Most vanadium is used to strengthen steel.

people.text: A peer-reviewed survey found vanadium contamination and health risk in farmland near vanadium smelters across China, with the highest soil levels at the Panzhihua smelting area. We found no reports on worker or community harm at Russian or South African vanadium operations. No record links a mine to EUROFER97.

harm.reason: Rated moderate: harm documented by 1 source.

stages.supplyReason: China and Russia hold about 94% of output.

steel.bottomLine: Fusion's structural steels come from a few European mills with no human rights hotspot found. Their alloying metals do not stop there: chromium comes partly from South African mines where protesters have faced violence, though no record links that chrome to fusion steel.
